units.heading: Von der Wermuot

clauses.source_assertion: Bitter herb, useful/accommodating to human nature; account attributed to Platearius and other masters.
Good against bodily worms, obstruction of liver/spleen, head illness from bad vapor; anticipatory use for falling illness termed apoplexia, and good remedy for loss of speech.
unpaid_or_ambiguous_arguments: no different stated outcome between wine-mixed and unmixed alternatives

clauses.source_assertion: Use prescribed for ear-worms.
Makes sight clear.

clauses.material: pronoun may continue juice or herb generally
clauses.operation_or_relation: protective relation, no application operation supplied
clauses.source_assertion: Protects for many years from worms and mice.
Good for and strengthens stomach and cooking/digestion of food.
unpaid_or_ambiguous_arguments: continuing material/route scope not separately restated

clauses.operation_or_relation: roast with oil; anoint body with it
clauses.source_assertion: Protects from fleas.

clauses.operation_or_relation: boil ink with it; write books/letters using treated ink
clauses.source_assertion: Mice do not gnaw the resulting writing.
unpaid_or_ambiguous_arguments: first anaphor may select herb or preceding preparation; no material composition chosen

clauses.recipient_or_endpoint: mites as hazard; treated substrate not supplied
clauses.source_assertion: Used against mites.

clauses.material: same named herb; its juice properties
clauses.operation_or_relation: opposed loosening/softening versus drawing together/making firm
clauses.source_assertion: First property attributed to heat/bitterness; second to coarseness of juice. Both asserted for the person needing the respective effect.
unpaid_or_ambiguous_arguments: no preparation switch isolating the two properties

clauses.source_assertion: Hot in first degree, dry in second degree; source classification, not measurement.
